messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital stay: The patient was admitted to the hospital due to the presence of a brain tumor located in the clivus region. He underwent surgical intervention via a left suboccipital craniotomy, which involved resection of the tumor. Oral intubation was done using the Macintosh laryngoscope blade, and the patient was placed in the left park bench position with neck flexion. Surgery was performed via the left lateral suboccipital approach. The lesion was decompressed, and the operation was completed successfully.

Medical Condition at Discharge: The patient had minor swelling in the neck, tongue, and pharynx on the left side. He experienced pain in the tip of his tongue with a small ulcer on the left side after returning to the intensive care unit. The swelling of his tongue gradually improved after the administration of steroids. The patient was discharged 10 days after the surgery.

Follow-Up Care: The patient was advised to undergo follow-up MRI after three months of surgery as well as clinical follow-up as per physician's recommendations.

Discharge Medications: None.

Instructions: The patient was advised to follow-up with his physician for regular check-up and take rest until complete recovery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is a brain tumour in the clivus region, which was resected by left suboccipital craniotomy. The histology is not stated. Clival tumours are most often chordoma or chondrosarcoma, but neither is confirmed here. A brain tumour of unspecified behaviour would fall under D49 (neoplasm of unspecified behaviour), in chapter D (neoplasms, which are in the C/D chapter). The clivus is a skull base bone, but with no histology, D49 is the most defensible category. The postoperative tongue swelling is a complication, not the reason for admission.

CODE: D49
